title: Event-lineage and version mapper for telemetry ingest
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Objective: implement an event-lineage mapping layer in the console backend ingestion pipeline that normalizes timestamps, annotates events with ingest-version metadata, and applies a configurable version-compatibility matrix for SDK/CLI/API clients. This is intended to make downstream analytics and cost attribution resilient to mixed client versions and transient clock skew while enabling a safe migration path for deprecated telemetry formats.
acceptance_criteria: Ingest pipeline attaches a stable 'lineage_id' to each event derived deterministically from client id + event_timestamp + schema_version, without using non-deterministic UUIDs
Events are annotated with 'client_schema_version' and 'ingest_resolution' headers visible in downstream parquet/warehouse tables
A version-compatibility matrix is stored in the config service (feature-flagged) and applies fallback transforms for up to two previous schema versions
Timestamp normalization resolves clock skew up to +/- 5 minutes using server-side heuristics and emits a 'timestamp_adjusted' boolean
Canary: 10% of traffic from mixed-version clients runs mapping layer with a 'dry-run' flag recorded in the audit log before full rollout
End-to-end tests + a small production canary prove no loss of event fidelity and no >1% increase in downstream transformation errors
progress_updates: 2025-02-11: Kickoff with Console backend, Data Eng, and SDK leads. Agreed on deterministic lineage_id scheme (sha1(client_id + iso_ts + schema_version)) and storage path in analytics parquet metadata.
2025-02-18: Draft of compatibility matrix format (CSV-backed config) completed. Data Eng suggested using a single-table mapping in config DB for fast lookups.
2025-02-21: Implemented PoC in local dev pipeline that annotates events and writes test parquet. Observed 0.8ms median overhead per event in PoC harness.
2025-02-25: Security review checklist submitted; KMS access required for lineage_id hashing keys. Security requested threat model for spoofed client_id cases.

2025-03-01: Integration tests added to CI with synthetic SDK v1/v2/v3 payloads; discovered edge-case where CLI batched events sent without per-event timestamps — added fallback to server_receive_time logic.
technical_decisions: lineage_id algorithm: SHA1(client_id || '|' || event_timestamp_iso || '|' || schema_version) truncated to 24 hex chars for storage efficiency
store client_schema_version as semantic-version string (e.g., 3.1.2) and map compatibility using major.minor rules in config table
timestamp normalization: prefer client_provided_timestamp when within 5 minutes of server_receive_time, otherwise set timestamp_adjusted=true and use server_receive_time
compatibility transforms executed in ingestion workers via small stateless lambdas to avoid large worker restarts
dry-run canary implemented with a 'mapping_mode' header: 'dry-run' | 'enforce' mapped to telemetry audit stream
test_plan: Unit tests for lineage_id generation and timestamp heuristics
Integration tests: run mixed-version payloads through staging pipeline validating parquet schema and metadata annotations
Load test: +20% events on staging ETL to validate CPU and latency impact (target <5% p95 add)
Canary plan: 10% dry-run for 48 hours, compare mapped vs raw event sets and alert on >0.5% transform discrepancy
Rollback criteria: any increase >2% in downstream consumer error rates or >1% data loss observed during canary
